body.text: What if you're already doing everything right?
You eat well. You take your vitamins. And you're still finding hair in the brush, in the shower and on your clothes.
Iron and biotin get all the airtime in these conversations. Potassium almost never does, and for some women it's the missing link.
How does a potassium deficiency trigger shedding?
Follicles behave like plants. They need the right environment before anything you feed them can be used.

When potassium runs low, sodium accumulates around the follicles. That buildup blocks the uptake of other nutrients, including iron and zinc, so the follicle ends up starving while surrounded by food.{cite:2}
The follicle ends up starving while surrounded by food.
A nutrient blockade is a stressor, and the body responds by moving hair out of its growing phase. That's telogen effluvium, the diffuse thinning across the whole scalp so many women describe.{cite:3}

How do you correct low potassium?
Food as the foundation
Spread potassium-rich foods across your day rather than relying on one item.
Supplementing, once testing shows a real deficit

Once a real deficit has built, diet alone often falls short, because absorption sets its own limit on what you actually take in.{cite:5} In our plans, potassium and magnesium are paired in capsule form, because magnesium helps the body use potassium, and they're supported with D3 for follicle health.{cite:6}

body.text: Talk to your doctor before supplementing potassium if you have kidney issues or take blood-pressure medication.

body.text: How long does it take to see a change?
It took months to deplete, so it takes months to replenish and let the hair cycle reset. That's biology, not a lack of effort on your part.
This type of shedding is usually temporary with a consistent plan. Most women can expect their hair to return toward its normal rhythm within about six months.{cite:7}
The real question is whether potassium is the whole story for you, or whether hormones, other nutrients or inflammation are also in play. That's what testing is for.

body.toc: What not to conclude from symptoms
body.text: What not to conclude from symptoms

Fatigue, cramping, sleep changes, palpitations, tingling, and shedding can each have more than one explanation. Seeing several together makes the potassium question worth asking. It does not make the answer automatic.
That distinction protects you from correcting the wrong thing. The history, scalp pattern, and focused testing have to agree before potassium belongs at the center of the plan.
Use symptoms to form a better question, not to choose your own dose.

faq.q: Can low potassium cause hair loss?
faq.a: It can contribute. When potassium runs low, sodium can build up around the follicles and block the uptake of nutrients like iron and zinc. That stress is commonly linked to telogen effluvium, a diffuse, all-over shedding.

faq.q: How long does it take for hair to grow back after fixing a potassium deficiency?
faq.a: It took months to deplete, so it takes months to replenish and let the hair cycle reset. With a consistent approach, most women can expect their hair to return toward its normal rhythm within about six months. Results not typical. Individual results will vary.

faq.q: What are the signs of low potassium?
faq.a: Unexplained fatigue, muscle weakness or cramping, trouble sleeping, heart palpitations, and tingling or numbness in the hands or feet. None of these is a diagnosis on its own. They are a reason to test.

faq.q: Should I take potassium supplements for hair loss?
faq.a: Only once testing shows a real deficit. Food is the foundation, but a significant deficiency often needs targeted correction. Talk to your doctor before supplementing potassium if you have kidney issues or take blood-pressure medication.

faq.q: What foods are highest in potassium?
faq.a: Melons, bananas, apricots, peaches, spinach, kale, mushrooms, broccoli, sweet potatoes, salmon, turkey, chicken, lima beans, black beans, brown rice, figs and raisins. Spread them across the day rather than relying on one item.

faq.q: Is potassium or biotin better for hair growth?
faq.a: Iron and biotin get most of the airtime, and potassium almost never does. For some women it is the missing link, which is why we test mineral status rather than guess.
